Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU pool — initial questions

Samantha — great to hear from you and glad the demo was helpful. Answers inline + next steps below.

1) Billing cadence and discounts:
- We support two billing profiles for Dedicated Reserved Commits: annual prepay (recommended for max discount tiers) and monthly invoicing (levelized) against a committed monthly SKU. Both can be contractually committed; the primary difference is the depth of discount. Annual prepay (prepaid full-year) gets the largest discount band (15–25% depending on pool size). Monthly-committed invoicing supports Net 30/Net 60 but has a slightly smaller discount (8–12%).

2) True-up / overage:
- True-ups are processed at the end of each billing period (monthly or quarterly per contract). If AtlasCloud exceeds committed throughput, we apply overage rates at the agreed per-token/per-second rate for the SKU. For large sustained overages (>25% sustained over a rolling quarter), we can convert the commitment to the next SKU effective the following month (with proration). We can include an automatic cap/fallback to avoid bill shock.

3) SKU sizing & throughput guarantees:
- Attached is a SKU matrix (RDW_Dedicated_Pricing_SKU_2026Q1.pdf) that maps GPU pool sizes (16/32/64 A100-equivalent GPUs), expected throughput (approx. tokens/sec and concurrent sessions), and 99th pct latency targets under typical batch settings. We guarantee throughput SLAs per SKU with credits for SLA violations; specifics are in the SOW.

Next steps:
- I attached a sample invoice layout and a draft SOW for AtlasCloud to review. If procurement prefers monthly invoices with Net 60, we can price a levelized monthly commit at the 10% discount band — I’ve asked Karthik to confirm margin flexibility for an additional 2–3% concession.

I'll follow up with a formal quote and a DocuSign link for a 12-month levelized commit and also a separate annual prepay option for comparison.

Best,
Ben Carter
